mainTopic: אגדות about the future: the לויתן, the glory of ירושלים, and the canopies of the צדיקים
overview: This amud is a long string of אגדות about the future. It begins with the לויתן: גבריאל will hunt it only with הקדוש ברוך הוא's help, its breath boils the sea, and its thirst leaves furrows that take seventy years to settle. רבה quotes רבי יוחנן that the צדיקים will feast on its meat, and the leftover meat will be sold in ירושלים. Its skin will become סוכות and smaller gifts according to each person's merit, and the rest will shine from the walls of ירושלים. The גמרא then explains ישעיהו 54:12. The walls will be of both onyx and jasper, and the gates will be giant jewels, as רבי יוחנן taught. A student who mocked that teaching saw angels cutting those very jewels and was punished. A ברייתא about how tall people will be in the future challenges the size of the gates, and the גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן meant wind-windows. The amud ends with canopies: seven for each צדיק, the meaning of their smoke and fire, the canopies of אדם הראשון in גן עדן, and the start of a פסוק about חירם מלך צור that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The hunt of the leviathan needs God's help
steps.stepSummary: The statement from the previous page ends here: גבריאל will hunt the לויתן, but he can only win because הקדוש ברוך הוא helps him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [גבריאל will one day make] a hunt with the לויתן, as the פסוק says: "Can you draw out the לויתן with a hook?" And if הקדוש ברוך הוא did not help him, he could not beat it, as it says: "Only He Who made him can bring His sword near him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence that began on the previous page. גבריאל will hunt the לויתן, and this succeeds only with God's help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים are used here. The first, "Can you draw out the לויתן with a hook?", shows that hunting the לויתן is something that will really happen. The second, "Only He Who made him can bring His sword near", shows that only its Creator can truly overpower it. That is why גבריאל needs הקדוש ברוך הוא's help.

keyTerms.meaning: A hunt, or a hunting contest
The giant sea creature described in ספר איוב
If not, or were it not for

phrases.english: a hunt with the leviathan,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: גבריאל is the one who will do this hunting.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Can you draw out leviathan with a hook
or press down his tongue with a rope?"
phrases.notes: איוב 40:25

phrases.english: And if the Holy One, Blessed be He, were not helping him,
phrases.notes: "Him" means גבריאל, the hunter.

phrases.english: he would not be able to beat it;
as it is said: "Only He Who made him can bring His sword near him."
phrases.notes: איוב 40:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement about גבריאל and the לויתן that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל will hunt the לויתן, but he will succeed only because הקדוש ברוך הוא helps him.

steps.title: When the leviathan is hungry, the sea boils
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings a teaching of רבי יוחנן: the hungry לויתן breathes out hot breath that boils the depths of the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When the לויתן is hungry, it breathes out from its mouth and boils all the waters of the deep. As it says: "He makes the deep boil like a pot."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching opens. רב דימי reports רבי יוחנן's description of how strong the hungry לויתן's breath is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the פסוק "He makes the deep boil like a pot." רבי יוחנן reads it literally. The לויתן's breath heats the whole deep sea the way fire heats a pot.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The deep part of the sea

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought teachings with him.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
At the time when the leviathan is hungry,
he lets out breath from his mouth
and boils all the waters in the deep,
as it is said: "He makes the deep boil like a pot."
phrases.notes: איוב 41:23

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hunt of the לויתן to a new description of its power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hungry לויתן's breath boils all the waters of the deep.

steps.title: The leviathan's smell and גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's teaching continues: the לויתן's smell is so strong that only putting its head into גן עדן keeps creatures alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the לויתן did not put its head into גן עדן, no creature could stand its smell. As it says: "He makes the sea like a spice mixture."
steps.whatsHappening: The same teaching of רבי יוחנן goes on, now about the לויתן's terrible smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the second half of the same פסוק. The word מרקחה is used for a mixture of spices, so the פסוק is read as speaking about smell. The good smell of גן עדן covers the לויתן's bad smell.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of spices or perfume

phrases.english: And if he did not put his head into the Garden of Eden,
no creature at all would be able
to stand his smell,
as it is said: "He makes the sea like a spice mixture."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, איוב 41:23. מרקחה is a word used for perfume, so the גמרא hears a hint about smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's teaching, using the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creatures can survive the לויתן's smell only because it puts its head into גן עדן.

steps.title: When the leviathan is thirsty, it furrows the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's teaching continues: when the לויתן is thirsty, it cuts deep furrows through the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when it is thirsty, it makes many furrows in the sea. As it says: "After him he lights up a path."
steps.whatsHappening: Still in רבי יוחנן's teaching, the גמרא now describes what the לויתן does when it is thirsty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the topic was hunger; now it is thirst. The פסוק about a shining path behind the לויתן is read as the long furrows it leaves in the water while it drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: Furrows, like the lines a plow cuts in a field

phrases.english: And at the time when he is thirsty,
he makes many furrows in the sea,
as it is said: "After him he lights up a path."
phrases.notes: איוב 41:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the hunger description in step 2, now about thirst.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirsty לויתן cuts many furrows through the sea.

steps.title: The sea needs seventy years to recover
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב adds that after the לויתן drinks, the deep sea takes seventy years to return to normal. He learns this from the word שיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The deep does not return to its normal state for seventy years. As it says: "One would think the deep to be gray-haired", and שיבה (gray old age) is no less than seventy.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא, רב אחא בר יעקב, adds to the furrows idea. He says how long the sea takes to recover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the next words of the same פסוק, which call the deep "gray-haired" (שיבה). שיבה means at least seventy years. So the deep stays disturbed for seventy years.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep, the depths of the sea

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
The deep does not return to its normal state
until seventy years [have passed],
as it is said: "One would think the deep to be gray-haired,"
phrases.notes: איוב 41:24

phrases.english: and "gray old age" is no less than seventy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to step 4: how long the disturbed sea takes to recover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the לויתן drinks, the deep takes seventy years to return to normal.

steps.title: A future feast of leviathan meat for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רבי יוחנן: in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a feast for the צדיקים from the לויתן's meat. The source is "יכרו עליו חברים".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a feast for the צדיקים from the meat of the לויתן. As it says: "The companions will make a feast of him."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: the famous future feast of the לויתן. The גמרא is setting up the next two steps, which prove the meaning of the key words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "יכרו עליו חברים" is not obviously about a feast or about צדיקים. The גמרא will now prove two things. כרה means a feast, and חברים means תלמידי חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future (here, the times of משיח)
They will make a feast (read by the גמרא as coming from כרה)

phrases.english: Rabbah said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will
make a feast for the righteous
from the meat of the leviathan,
as it is said: "The companions will make a feast of him";
phrases.notes: איוב 40:30. The next two lines show why each word means what the גמרא says.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לויתן's nature to its role in the future reward of the צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a feast for the צדיקים from the לויתן's meat.

steps.title: Proving that the word means a feast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from ספר מלכים that the word כרה means a feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: And כרה means nothing other than a feast, as it says: "And he prepared for them a great feast (כרה), and they ate and drank."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first part of the reading. The word יכרו in the פסוק really refers to a feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מלכים ב, the same root (כרה) clearly means a meal, because the פסוק continues "they ate and drank." So in איוב too, יכרו עליו means making a feast out of the לויתן.

keyTerms.meaning: Means nothing other than (a formula for defining a word)

phrases.english: And "kerah" means nothing other than a feast,
as it is said: "And he prepared for them a great feast,
and they ate and drank";
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 6:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first key word of the פסוק quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That יכרו in איוב 40:30 refers to making a feast.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 6:23, where כרה is followed by eating and drinking.

steps.title: Proving that the companions are Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from שיר השירים that חברים means תלמידי חכמים, so the feast is for the צדיקים who learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חברים means nothing other than תלמידי חכמים, as it says: "You who sit in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice: let me hear it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second part of the reading. The חברים who will eat the feast are תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שיר השירים, the חברים are the ones who listen closely for the voice, which the גמרא understands as people who listen to God's word, meaning תלמידי חכמים. With both words proven, the פסוק in איוב reads: the תלמידי חכמים will feast on the לויתן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's teaching is built from two word-proofs. כרה means a feast (מלכים ב), and חברים means תלמידי חכמים (שיר השירים). Together they turn "יכרו עליו חברים" into the future feast of the לויתן for the צדיקים.

phrases.english: And "companions" means nothing other than Torah scholars,
as it is said: "You who sit in the gardens,
the companions listen for your voice: let me hear it."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 8:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second key word of the פסוק from step 6, completing the reading.
steps.raayaObject: That חברים in איוב 40:30 refers to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 8:13, where the חברים listen closely for the voice.

steps.title: The leftover meat is sold in the markets of Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's teaching continues. Whatever is left of the לויתן after the feast is divided up and sold in the markets of ירושלים, based on the פסוק "יחצוהו בין כנענים".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rest of it, they divide it up and do business with it in the markets of ירושלים, as it says: "They will divide him among the כנענים."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי יוחנן's teaching about the feast. It says that the meat left over after the צדיקים eat will be divided and sold in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the צדיקים will feast on the לויתן's meat. Now we learn what happens to the leftovers: they become merchandise. The source is the word כנענים in the פסוק, which the גמרא will explain in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And the rest, meaning what is left over

phrases.english: And the rest, they divide it up,
phrases.notes: "The rest" means the לויתן's meat left over after the צדיקים' feast in step 6.

phrases.english: and do business with it in the markets of Jerusalem,
as it says: "They will divide him among the kena'anim."
phrases.notes: איוב 40:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's feast teaching from steps 6-8 by explaining what happens to the leftover meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover meat of the לויתן will be divided and sold in the markets of ירושלים.

steps.title: Proof that כנענים means merchants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from הושע that the word כנען means a merchant. So "dividing among the כנענים" means selling to merchants.
steps.simpleTranslation: And כנענים means nothing other than merchants, as it says: "A merchant (כנען) has scales of cheating in his hand; he loves to rob."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק in step 9 is about business. It shows from another פסוק that the word כנען means a merchant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally כנענים means the nation of כנען. But in the פסוק in הושע, כנען describes someone holding cheating scales, which is a picture of a merchant. That shows that "dividing among the כנענים" means selling in the market.

phrases.english: And kena'anim means nothing other than merchants,
as it says: "A merchant (kena'an) has scales of cheating in his hand,
he loves to rob."
phrases.notes: הושע 12:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the meaning of the key word כנענים from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That כנענים in the פסוק in איוב means merchants.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 12:8: "כנען בידו מאזני מרמה", where כנען is clearly a merchant with scales.

steps.title: A second proof that כנענים means merchants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another proof from ישעיהו, where כנעניה is set side by side with סוחריה (her traders).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say the proof is from here: "Whose traders are princes, whose merchants (כנעניה) are the honored ones of the land."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second proof for the same point: כנען means merchant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק the two halves say the same thing in different words. "Her traders" (סוחריה) in the first half matches "her כנענים" in the second half. That shows the two words mean the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another option or proof)

phrases.english: And if you want, say the proof is from here:
"Whose traders are princes,
whose merchants (kinaneha) are the honored ones of the land."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 23:8. The second half repeats the first, so כנעניה matches "her traders".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative proof for the same point as step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 23:8, where כנעניה is set beside סוחריה.

steps.title: A סוכה for the צדיקים from the לויתן's skin
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רבי יוחנן: in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a סוכה for the צדיקים out of the לויתן's skin. The source is "התמלא בשכות עורו".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a סוכה for the צדיקים from the skin of the לויתן, as it says: "Can you fill his skin with sukkot?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the לויתן's meat to its skin. A new teaching says the skin will become a סוכה for the צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the word שכות in the פסוק, which sounds like סוכות. Since the פסוק links שכות to עורו (his skin), רבי יוחנן learns that the skin will be made into סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: With barbed irons; here read as sounding like סוכות

phrases.english: And Rabba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת סוּכָּה לַצַּדִּיקִים
phrases.english: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make a sukka for the righteous
from the skin of the leviathan,
as it says: "Can you fill his skin with sukkot?"
phrases.notes: איוב 40:31. The word שכות sounds like סוכות, and that is the hint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same chain (רבה quoting רבי יוחנן), moving from the meat to the skin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, the צדיקים will receive a סוכה made from the לויתן's skin.

steps.title: Smaller gifts for those less deserving
steps.stepSummary: The size of each person's piece of skin depends on how deserving he is: a whole סוכה, then a head covering (צלצל), then a necklace (ענק), then an amulet (קמיע). Each level has its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is deserving, they make him a סוכה. If not, they make him a head covering, as it says: "And his head with fish-spears (צלצל)." If he is deserving, a head covering. If not, a necklace, as it says: "And necklaces for your neck." If he is deserving, a necklace. If not, an amulet, as it says: "Will you tie him for your young girls?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that not everyone gets a whole סוכה. Each person gets a piece of the skin that fits his level, going down step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four levels, from biggest to smallest: סוכה, צלצל (head covering), ענק (necklace), and קמיע (amulet). Each smaller level is hinted at in a פסוק. The pattern "זכה... לא זכה" repeats, and each time it moves one level down.

keyTerms.meaning: He is deserving, he earned it
A head covering (in the פסוק: fish-spears)
An amulet, a small item tied on the body

steps.confusionAlert: "לא זכה" here does not mean he gets nothing. He is still one of the people getting a gift; he just gets the next smaller item.

phrases.english: If he is deserving, they make him a sukka;
if he is not deserving, they make him a head covering,
as it says: "And his head with fish-spears (tziltzal)."
phrases.notes: איוב 40:31, the second half of the same פסוק from step 12.

phrases.english: If he is deserving, they make him a head covering;
if he is not deserving, they make him a necklace,
as it says: "And necklaces for your neck."
phrases.notes: משלי 1:9

phrases.english: If he is deserving, they make him a necklace;
if he is not deserving, they make him an amulet,
as it says: "Will you tie him for your young girls?"
phrases.notes: איוב 40:29. Something small that is tied on, like an amulet tied on a child.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָה – עוֹשִׂין לוֹ סוּכָּה, לֹא זָכָה – עוֹשִׂין לוֹ צִלְצָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 12 by explaining what people who don't earn a full סוכה receive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person receives a piece of the לויתן's skin that matches his merit: a סוכה, a head covering, a necklace, or an amulet.

steps.title: The rest of the skin shines from the walls of Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The leftover skin is spread by הקדוש ברוך הוא over the walls of ירושלים, and its brightness shines from one end of the world to the other, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rest, הקדוש ברוך הוא spreads it over the walls of ירושלים, and its shine glows from one end of the world to the other, as it says: "And nations will walk by your light, and kings by the brightness of your shining."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the teaching about the לויתן's skin. Whatever skin is left will cover the walls of ירושלים and light up the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels step 9: there the leftover meat went to the markets of ירושלים, and here the leftover skin goes on the walls of ירושלים. The פסוק about nations walking by ירושלים's light is the source for the skin's worldwide glow.
steps.whatToRemember: Nothing from the לויתן is wasted. The meat feeds the צדיקים and the rest is sold in ירושלים. The skin becomes סוכות and smaller gifts based on merit, and the rest lights up the world from the walls of ירושלים.

phrases.english: And the rest, the Holy One, Blessed be He, spreads it
phrases.notes: "The rest" here means the leftover skin, not the meat from step 9.

phrases.english: over the walls of Jerusalem,
and its shine glows
from one end of the world to the other end,
as it says: "And nations will walk by your light,
and kings by the brightness of your shining."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְּׁאָר – פּוֹרְסוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל חוֹמוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the skin teaching by saying what happens to the skin left over after all the gifts in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover skin of the לויתן will be spread over the walls of ירושלים, and its light will shine across the whole world.

steps.title: What the walls of Jerusalem will be made of: onyx, jasper, or both
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains the word כדכד. Two angels, or two אמוראים, argue whether it means שוהם or ישפה. הקדוש ברוך הוא says: let it be both, כדין וכדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "I will make your pinnacles of כדכד." רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: two angels in heaven argue about this, גבריאל and מיכאל. Some say it is two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל who argue, יהודה and חזקיה, the sons of רבי חייא. One says it means onyx, and one says jasper. הקדוש ברוך הוא said to them: let it be like this one and like that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a פסוק in ישעיהו about the future walls of ירושלים. It explains the strange word כדכד through a disagreement that הקדוש ברוך הוא settles by saying both are right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rare word כדכד is read as a combination of כדין (like this) and כדין (like that). That reading explains the word itself: the stones will be a mix of both kinds that were suggested. The גמרא gives two versions of who argued: angels in heaven, or two sons of רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: A rare word in the פסוק, explained here as a mix of two precious stones
Your pinnacles or battlements, the top parts of the walls
Literally "the West"; the גמרא's name for ארץ ישראל
Like this and like that, meaning both

phrases.english: "And I will make your pinnacles of kadkhod"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:12

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
Two angels in heaven disagree
Gabriel and Michael;
and some say it is two amora'im in the West,
phrases.notes: "The West" is how the גמרא refers to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and who are they?
Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya, the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: שׁוֹהַם, וְחַד אָמַר: יָשְׁפֵה.
phrases.english: one said: onyx, and one said: jasper.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Let it be like this and like that.
phrases.notes: Put כדין and כדין together and you hear the word כדכד from the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׂמְתִּי כַּדְכֹד שִׁמְשֹׁתַיִךְ אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 14 described the לויתן skin spread on the walls of ירושלים. This step stays with the theme of ירושלים's future glory. It brings a different פסוק (ישעיהו 54:12) about what the walls themselves will be made of.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word כדכד means the walls will be made of both שוהם and ישפה, because הקדוש ברוך הוא said 'כדין וכדין'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the gates will be giant carved jewels
steps.stepSummary: On the words "and your gates of אבני אקדח", רבי יוחנן teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring jewels 30 by 30 אמות, carve a 10 by 20 opening in each one, and set them up as the gates of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And your gates of precious stones": this fits what רבי יוחנן taught. In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring precious stones and pearls that are thirty by thirty, carve into them an opening ten by twenty, and set them up in the gates of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the same פסוק by quoting a teaching of רבי יוחנן about how the gates of ירושלים will be built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each gate will be one single jewel. It will be 30 by 30 אמות, with a doorway 10 wide and 20 high cut into it. This teaching also sets up the story that comes next, about a student who could not believe it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shining precious stones, from the פסוק
Was teaching or explaining a פסוק in public

phrases.english: "And your gates of precious stones"

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְקָא דָרֵישׁ:
phrases.english: like that time when Rabbi Yoḥanan sat and taught:
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring
precious stones and pearls
that are thirty by thirty,
phrases.notes: The measurements are in אמות (cubits).

phrases.english: and He will carve in them an opening of ten by twenty,
and set them up in the gates of Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁעָרַיִךְ לְאַבְנֵי אֶקְדָּח כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְקָא דָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק (ישעיהו 54:12), moving from the walls to the gates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gates of ירושלים will be single jewels 30 by 30 אמות, with a 10 by 20 opening carved into each.

steps.title: A student mocks רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: A student laughs at רבי יוחנן: today we cannot even find a jewel the size of a dove's egg, so how could there be jewels that huge?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain student mocked him: Now we cannot even find a jewel the size of a dove's egg, and we will find one this big?!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, a student pushes back against רבי יוחנן's teaching by mocking it as impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is based only on what he can see today. Even small jewels are rare, so in his eyes giant ones are ridiculous. This is not a respectful question. It is a sneer, and the rest of the story shows how wrong that attitude is.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg of a dove, a small size

phrases.english: A certain student mocked him:
Now, even the size of a dove's egg
we do not find,
and this much we will find?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's teaching about giant jewel gates.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that each gate will be one jewel 30 by 30 אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jewels even the size of a dove's egg are rare today, so jewels that huge seem impossible.

steps.title: The student sees angels cutting the giant jewels
steps.stepSummary: Later, on a sea voyage, the student sees angels sawing jewels exactly 30 by 30 with a 10 by 20 opening. They tell him these are for the gates of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some time later his ship sailed out to sea. He saw ministering angels sitting and sawing precious stones and pearls that were thirty by thirty, with an opening ten by twenty carved into them. He said to them: Who are these for? They told him: הקדוש ברוך הוא will set them up in the gates of ירושלים in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that רבי יוחנן was right: the student himself sees the exact stones that were described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measurements match רבי יוחנן's words exactly, 30 by 30 with a 10 by 20 opening, and the angels confirm what the stones are for. So the very person who mocked the teaching ends up seeing it with his own eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: His ship sailed out to sea

phrases.english: Some time later, his ship sailed out to sea,
he saw ministering angels
who were sitting and sawing
precious stones and pearls
that were thirty by thirty,
and carved in them was an opening ten wide and twenty high.
He said to them: Who are these for?
They said to him:
that in the future the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will set them up in the gates of Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the student's mockery by showing the giant stones really exist.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the giant jewel gates
steps.raayaSupportSource: The student's own sighting of angels cutting stones of exactly those measurements, and the angels' explanation

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rebukes and punishes the student
steps.stepSummary: The student comes back and praises רבי יוחנן, saying he saw it himself. רבי יוחנן calls him worthless: you believed only because you saw, so you were mocking the חכמים. He looks at him, and the student becomes a heap of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי יוחנן and said to him: Teach, my teacher, it is fitting for you to teach. Just as you said, so I saw. רבי יוחנן said to him: Empty one! If you had not seen, you would not have believed. You are a mocker of the words of the חכמים! He set his eyes on him, and he became a heap of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The student's praise is rejected, and he is punished for having mocked the words of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student thinks his praise fixes things. רבי יוחנן points out that it actually shows the problem: he trusted only his own eyes and not the teaching of the חכמים. The story closes the explanation of "your gates of אבני אקדח."

keyTerms.meaning: It is fitting for you to teach
He set his eyes on him (a look that punishes)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the jewel gates is confirmed. The story's lesson is that a person must trust the words of the חכמים even before seeing proof.

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and said to him: Teach, my teacher,
it is fitting for you to teach,
just as you said, so I saw.
He said to him: Empty one!
If you had not seen, you would not have believed;
you are a mocker of the words of the Sages!
He set his eyes upon him,
and he became a heap of bones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story that began with the student's mockery in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's teaching stands, and mocking the words of the חכמים is severely wrong even if the mocker later sees the truth.

steps.title: Challenge: people in the future will be 200 cubits tall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי מאיר reads קוממיות as two קומות, meaning people will be 200 אמות tall, twice the height of אדם הראשון. This sets up a challenge to רבי יוחנן's 20-אמה-high gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא: "And I will lead you upright (קוממיות)." רבי מאיר says: two hundred אמות, like two heights of אדם הראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבי יוחנן. Here it only quotes the ברייתא, and the actual question is spelled out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר hears the word קוממיות as two קומות (heights), so people in the future will be 200 אמות tall. If so, a gate opening only 20 אמות high, as רבי יוחנן said, seems far too small for them to walk through.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, usually from a ברייתא
Heights, how tall a person is

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mention gates at all. The challenge works only by putting the two together: 200-אמה people and a 20-אמה doorway.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And I will lead you upright"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:13

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: two hundred cubits,
like two heights of Adam the first man.
phrases.notes: He hears קוממיות as two קומות. אדם הראשון was 100 אמות tall, so two of him is 200.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's measurements from step 16 and starts to challenge them.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the gate opening will be 20 אמות high
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people will be 200 אמות tall, a 20-אמה-high gate would be far too low for them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: People will be 100 cubits tall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה says people will be 100 אמות tall, like the היכל and its walls. This finishes the challenge against רבי יוחנן's gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: people will be one hundred אמות tall, matching the height of the היכל and its walls. As the פסוק says: 'Our sons are like saplings grown tall in their youth, our daughters like carved corner-pillars, shaped like the היכל.' So how could people this tall fit through gates only 20 אמות high?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. רבי יהודה's view, 100 אמות tall, makes the problem with רבי יוחנן's 20-אמה gates even clearer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether people are 200 אמות tall (רבי מאיר) or 100 אמות tall (רבי יהודה), they are far taller than a 20-אמה gate. The exclamation at the end is the real challenge: רבי יוחנן's gate measurements don't seem to fit people that size.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש, 100 אמות tall

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one hundred cubits,
corresponding to the Sanctuary and its walls,
as it is stated: "We whose sons are like saplings
grown up in their youth;
our daughters are like carved corner-pillars
in the form of the Sanctuary"!
phrases.notes: תהלים 144:12. The question is: how could people that tall walk through 20-אמה gates?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 20 and lands the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the gates of ירושלים will be 10 by 20 אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people will be 100 or 200 אמות tall, a 20-אמה-high gate is far too small for them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן meant the wind-windows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's 10-by-20 openings are wind-windows, not the main gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said 10 by 20, he was talking about the windows that let the wind in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוחנן's measurements were for small air-windows, not for the gates people walk through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only existed if the 10-by-20 opening was the entrance. By moving his statement to windows, the size no longer has to fit tall people, so both the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן can stand.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said it,
it was about the windows for the wind.
phrases.notes: Literally "windows of the house of wind": openings that let air in, not the doorways people walk through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 20-21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the statement was talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן's 10-by-20 opening was the main gate people walk through.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 10-by-20 opening is a wind-window, so it doesn't need to fit 100- or 200-אמה-tall people.

steps.title: Seven canopies for every righteous person
steps.stepSummary: רבה quoting רבי יוחנן: in the future, ה' will make seven canopies for each צדיק, each matched to his honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make seven canopies for every single צדיק. As the פסוק says: 'ה' will create over all of Mount Zion and over those invited there a cloud by day, and smoke and the shine of flaming fire by night, for over all the glory there will be a canopy.' This teaches that ה' makes each person a canopy that fits his level of honor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רבי יוחנן says every צדיק will get canopies in the future, sized to his honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'over all the glory a canopy' are read as: each person's glory gets its own canopy. Because it depends on his honor, different people get different canopies, and the next steps build on that difference.

phrases.english: And Rabba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will make seven canopies
for each and every righteous person,
as it is stated: "And the Lord will create
over the whole site of Mount Zion
and over those invited to it, a cloud by day,
and smoke, and the shine of a flaming fire by night;
for over all the glory shall be a canopy"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 4:5

phrases.english: This teaches that for each and every one
the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes for him
a canopy according to his honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת שֶׁבַע חוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה from רבי יוחנן in the same series about the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every צדיק will receive canopies from ה' in the future, each according to his own honor.

steps.title: Why is there smoke in a canopy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק puts smoke into a canopy of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would there be smoke in a canopy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about one detail of the פסוק. This question sets up רבי חנינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A canopy is supposed to be an honor, but smoke is unpleasant. So the גמרא wants to know what the smoke is doing there.

phrases.english: Smoke in the canopy, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose the smoke in the canopy serves

steps.title: Smoke for those who begrudged Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא: whoever was stingy toward תלמידי חכמים in this world gets his eyes filled with smoke in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: anyone who looks at תלמידי חכמים with narrow, begrudging eyes in this world will have his eyes filled with smoke in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question: the smoke is a punishment for people who begrudged תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment matches the sin: the eyes that were 'narrow' toward scholars now fill with smoke. The smoke is not for the צדיק inside the canopy; it is for the one who resented him.

keyTerms.meaning: Narrow eyes: being stingy or begrudging

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Because anyone whose eyes are narrow
phrases.notes: "Narrow eyes" means stingy or resentful, not wanting good for someone.

phrases.english: toward Torah scholars in this world,
his eyes fill with smoke in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שֶׁכׇּל מִי שֶׁעֵינָיו צָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The smoke fills the eyes of those who begrudged תלמידי חכמים in this world.

steps.title: Why is there fire in a canopy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק puts fire in a canopy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why would there be fire in a canopy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a second detail of the same פסוק, setting up רבי חנינא's next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the smoke, fire seems out of place in a canopy of honor, so the גמרא asks what it means.

phrases.english: And fire in the canopy, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to step 24, about the fire instead of the smoke.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose the fire in the canopy serves

steps.title: Burned by a friend's bigger canopy
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא: each person is 'burned' by his friend's canopy, embarrassed that his own is smaller. Woe for that shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: this teaches that each person gets burned by his friend's canopy. Woe for that shame, woe for that disgrace!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא explains the fire: each צדיק feels a burning embarrassment when he sees that someone else got a greater canopy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on step 23: canopies are 'according to his honor,' so they are not all equal. The fire is the pain of comparing, the shame of not having earned more.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
This teaches that each and every one
is burned by the canopy of his friend.
phrases.notes: Burned with embarrassment: his friend's canopy is greater than his own.

phrases.english: Woe for that shame,
woe for that disgrace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נִכְוֶה מֵחוּפָּתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire is the burning shame each person feels seeing a friend's greater canopy.

steps.title: משה like the sun, יהושע like the moon
steps.stepSummary: A similar idea: משה gave only some of his splendor to יהושע. The elders said משה's face was like the sun, יהושע's like the moon. Woe for that shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way you can explain: 'And you shall put of your splendor on him.' Of your splendor, but not all of your splendor. The elders of that generation said: משה's face was like the sun, יהושע's face was like the moon. Woe for that shame, woe for that disgrace!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel case of the same feeling of shame from a difference in greatness: the gap between משה and יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter מ in 'מֵהוֹדְךָ' means 'some of,' so יהושע got only part of משה's splendor. The elders' cry of 'woe' matches the same words used about the canopies: the pain of seeing a lesser level next to a greater one.
steps.whatToRemember: The future canopies are given according to each person's honor, and seeing someone else's greater level brings real shame. The same lesson shows in משה (the sun) and יהושע (the moon).

phrases.english: Similar to this, you say:
"And you shall put of your splendor upon him"
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:20. ה' is telling משה what to give יהושע.

phrases.english: but not all of your splendor;
the elders of that generation said:
The face of Moshe was like the face of the sun,
the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon;
woe for that shame,
woe for that disgrace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel example of the same shame described in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע received only part of משה's splendor, and the elders felt shame at that drop in greatness.

steps.title: Ten canopies for the first man
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא teaches that הקב״ה made ten canopies for אדם הראשון in גן עדן, learned from the list of precious materials in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא says: הקדוש ברוך הוא made ten canopies for אדם הראשון in גן עדן, as it says: 'You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about canopies. Earlier the גמרא spoke about the canopies of צדיקים in the future, and now it says אדם הראשון also had canopies in גן עדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל lists ten materials, starting with precious stones and ending with gold. רבי חמא בר חנינא reads each item as a separate canopy, so he gets ten.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina says:
Ten canopies were made
by the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the first man
in the Garden of Eden,
as it is stated: "You were in Eden, the garden of God;
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 28:13. The פסוק goes on to list ten materials, ending with gold.

phrases.english: every precious stone, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: עֶשֶׂר חוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the canopies of צדיקים in the future to the canopies of אדם הראשון in גן עדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה made ten canopies for אדם הראשון, one for each material listed in the פסוק.

steps.title: מר זוטרא counts eleven canopies
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says there were eleven canopies, because the words 'every precious stone' count as one more.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Eleven, as it says: 'Every precious stone.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא disagrees with the count of ten and says there were eleven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that each listed material is a canopy. מר זוטרא adds the opening words 'every precious stone' as an extra canopy, which brings the total to eleven.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: Eleven,
as it is stated: "Every precious stone."
phrases.notes: He counts these opening words as one more canopy, added to the ten items in the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different count of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were eleven canopies, because 'every precious stone' is counted as well.

steps.title: Gold was the least valuable canopy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says gold was the lowest of all the canopies, since the פסוק lists it last.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And the worst of all of them was gold, since it is counted last.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a detail about the list: gold was the least valuable canopy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the order of the list as a ranking. Because gold comes last, it must be worth less than the precious stones listed before it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And the worst of all of them was gold,
since it counts it last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ranking to the list of canopies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold was the least valuable canopy because it is listed last.

steps.title: What do 'your drums and your holes' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the next words in the same פסוק mean: 'the workmanship of your drums and your holes in you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'The workmanship of your drums and your holes was in you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק and asks about a puzzling phrase in it. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the list of jewels, the פסוק suddenly talks about 'drums' and 'holes.' The גמרא wants to know what holes have to do with this message.

phrases.english: What is "The workmanship of your drums
and your holes in you"?
phrases.notes: נקביך comes from נקב, a hole. That word is the key to the answer that follows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'drums and holes' in יחזקאל 28:13.

steps.title: I made many openings in man because of you
steps.stepSummary: רב says הקב״ה told חירם מלך צור: 'I looked at you, and created many openings in man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says that רב says: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to חירם מלך צור: 'I looked at you, and I created many, many openings in man.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The 'holes' are the openings הקב״ה made in the human body, and He made them with חירם in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is addressed to חירם מלך צור. רב reads 'your holes' as the many openings in the human body. This is commonly explained as a reminder that a person, even one who calls himself a god as חירם did, is only a human being with bodily needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiram, king of Tyre, the one the פסוק is speaking to

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said
to Hiram, king of Tyre:
"I looked at you,
and I created many, many openings in man."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחִירָם מֶלֶךְ צוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'your holes.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Your holes' are the many openings הקב״ה created in man, made with חירם in mind.

steps.title: A second version of what הקב״ה told חירם
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב's explanation differently. It also opens with 'I looked at you,' and the rest continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say that this is what He said: 'I looked at you,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second version of רב's explanation. Only the opening words appear here, and the full explanation continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions begin with 'I looked at you.' They differ in what הקב״ה says came next. So far only the shared opening appears, so the difference has not been shown yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And there are those who say, introducing another version

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of a sentence. Do not treat 'I looked at you' as the whole second version. The new part is still to come.

phrases.english: And there are those who say,
this is what He said:
I looked at you,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָכִי קָאָמַר: בְּךָ נִסְתַּכַּלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a different report of רב's answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second version of רב's explanation, which also opens with 'I looked at you.' The rest continues on the next part of the daf.
